original.guitar: Acoustic rhythm guitar (band guitarists over the years include Gilles Cartin, André Marchand and Michel Bordeleau; track credits not found)
original.notes: Traditional Quebec music: accordion, fiddle, foot-tapping (podorythmie) and acoustic guitar. The album and players on this track were not confirmed.

recipes.tips: In Quebec trad music the guitar is the rhythm section: strong, percussive strumming that locks in with the foot-tapping, with accents on the off-beats and bass notes alternating on the downbeats. Channel A is brighter and more percussive, channel B a bit warmer. Leave the melody to the accordion and fiddle.
recipes.why: The guitar on these recordings is acoustic. The ACOUSTIC effect into a very clean amp, with a short room reverb, gets an electric close to a strummed acoustic. The brighter treble setting helps the strumming cut through accordion and fiddle.

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: La Bottine souriante

original.notes: For playing the song with a plain electric sound instead of the acoustic simulation.

recipes.tips: Channel A is a plain, clean electric for percussive strumming. Channel B is a warmer AC15 with a touch of grit. There's no delay, so fast strumming stays tight: add the slapback (DELAY) only if the room sounds dead.
recipes.why: If you'd rather sound like an electric guitar, a clean, lightly compressed amp with a short room reverb keeps the fast trad rhythm crisp and out of the way of the accordion and fiddle.
